title: A Collective-Spin Derivation of the Uniform Magnon Hamiltonian in Cavity Magnonics
authors: Tomas Aguiar, Marcos Cesar de Oliveira
abstract: We present a direct collective-spin derivation of the effective uniform-mode Hamiltonian used in cavity magnonics. Starting from a nearest-neighbor Heisenberg ferromagnet coupled to long-wavelength magnetic fields, we show that the relevant dynamics can be restricted to the fully symmetric spin sector, where the exchange interaction contributes only a constant energy shift and the ferromagnet behaves as a macrospin of length $Ns$. Applying the Holstein--Primakoff transformation directly to this total spin yields the usual uniform magnon mode and its leading nonlinear corrections without first introducing site-resolved bosonic operators. This collective formulation makes explicit the interpretation of the ferromagnet as a synthetic large-spin atom and provides a compact route to the effective Hamiltonians used in driven and Floquet cavity magnonics. As a physical consequence, the leading nonlinear correction produces an occupation-dependent reduction of the effective magnon--photon coupling, providing a simple signature of finite-spin saturation under strong uniform-mode driving.
summary: This paper develops a novel theoretical framework using a collective-spin approach to derive the effective Hamiltonian governing uniform magnon excitations in cavity magnonics. By treating the ferromagnet as a single large spin, the authors simplify the derivation significantly compared to site-resolved methods. The key finding is the prediction of an occupation-dependent reduction in the magnon-photon coupling when the system approaches finite-spin saturation under strong driving.
main_problem: The paper aims to derive an effective Hamiltonian for uniform magnon dynamics in cavity magnonics using a novel collective-spin approach, bypassing the standard site-resolved bosonic operator method.
main_result: The collective formulation successfully yields the effective uniform-mode Hamiltonian and predicts that strong driving leads to an occupation-dependent reduction of the magnon-photon coupling due to finite-spin saturation effects.
method: It employs a direct Holstein-Primakoff transformation applied to the total spin ($\mathbf{S}$) of the ferromagnet, treating it as a single macrospin, contrasting this with the conventional site-resolved approach.
model_or_system: The system is a ferromagnetic sample modeled by a Heisenberg Hamiltonian coupled to external magnetic fields (static bias and cavity drives). The dynamics are analyzed in the long-wavelength limit, focusing on the uniform magnon mode.
key_observables: Effective magnon-photon coupling strength ($G_{	ext{eff}}$), occupation number ($ ar{n}_M$), and the resulting nonlinear correction factor.
important_parameters: The total spin $S=Ns$, the low-excitation regime condition ($\langle\hat{M}^\dagger \hat{M}angle \ll 2N_s$), and the ratio of cavity wavelength to sample size.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system is near its fully polarized ground state, that dynamics are dominated by the uniform mode (long-wavelength limit), and neglects surface or non-uniform dipolar effects.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes; the focus is on deriving and comparing Hamiltonian forms (Eq. 9 vs Eq. 17/20) and showing the nonlinear correction formula (Eq. 35).
paper_structure: The paper contrasts the standard site-resolved approach with the proposed collective-spin derivation, demonstrating their equivalence for the uniform mode while highlighting the conceptual simplicity of the macrospin treatment.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical tool—the collective spin description—to model magnon dynamics in cavity QED settings. The explicit inclusion of finite-size/finite-spin effects is crucial for accurately predicting nonlinear interactions under strong coherent driving, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and circuit QED.
